line_facts.fact: initHardware(IOService *provider) is protected pure virtual bool; start(IOService*) and free() override IOService.
getPageSize(void) const returns uint64_t and is pure virtual.
iovmMapMemory(memory, descriptorOffset,length,mapOptions,mapSpecification,dmaCommand,pageList,mapAddress,mapLength) -> IOReturn. All uint64_t extents/offsets here are bytes, unlike the C wrappers.

iovmUnmapMemory(IOMemoryDescriptor*,IODMACommand*,uint64_t mapAddress,uint64_t mapLength) -> IOReturn; iovmInsert(uint32_t options,uint64_t mapAddress,uint64_t offset,uint64_t physicalAddress,uint64_t length) -> IOReturn; mapToPhysicalAddress(uint64_t) -> uint64_t. All are pure virtual.

Base start calls super then initHardware; gets page size, asserts <=UINT_MAX and caches it. fIsSystem publishes gSystem if true. It copies provider iommu-id, else AAPL,phandle, to IOMapperID. It does not call registerService. Base free merely calls super.

copyMapperForDeviceWithIndex first reads device iommu-parent. Missing -> NULL; an IOMapper object is retained directly. OSData is indexed as UInt32 and converted to a four-byte OSData property match; out-of-range index -> NULL. Non-OSData matches the original object type. It waits for matching IOMapper without a timeout argument.
gIOMapperIDKey is initialized from literal IOMapperID (IOService.cpp:533); property type/value must match, not just the numeric appearance.
waitForMatchingService(matching,timeout=UINT64_MAX) returns a retained OSPtr; default wait is forever. Do not call device mapper lookup while holding the lock/gate needed by publication.

System mapper sentinels and wait state are separate from per-device lookup; IOPlatformExpert.cpp:157 sets required based on platform mapper-present property. A per-requester adapter must not change global presence or assign gSystem.
C IOMapperIOVMAlloc/Free/InsertPage operate on gSystem, convert page counts with ptoa_64, omit device ownership and discard unmap/insert status. They are not the safe per-device ownership interface.

IODMAMapSpecification = uint64 alignment, IOService*device, uint32 options, uint8 numAddressBits, resvA[3], resvB[4]. IODMAMapPageList = uint32 pageOffset,pageListCount; const upl_page_info_t*pageList.

Map options: Read1,Write2,PhysicallyContiguous0x10,DeviceMemory0x20,PagingPath0x40,IdentityMap0x80,PageListFullyOccupied0x100,FixedAddress0x200. Do not conflate these with IODMACommand MappingOptions kMapped/kBypassed/kNonCoherent/kUnmapped.
Generic dmaMap derives Read access plus Write unless PreparedReadOnly, passes original mapSpec and NULL pageList, records returned mapLength on success.

IOGeneralMemoryDescriptor starts mapAddress=0; HostOnly returns success with no mapper call, Remote returns NotAttached. Physical descriptors, offset!=0 or non-entire length use generic path. Whole virtual/page-backed path passes a new zeroed mapSpec with only accumulated numAddressBits/alignment; caller device/options/reserved values are not carried through.

Page-list path passes pageOffset, _pages and upl entries. External UPL marks PagingPath. FullyOccupied requires _length==ptoa(_pages) and aligned first offset. fDMAAccess supplies permissions. On-device IOPL adds PhysicallyContiguous.
Passing a non-IOMapper object in mapper slot records it as device then sets mapper NULL; a missing mapper outside kUnmapped falls back to gSystem. kMapped alone is not proof that a mapper exists.
Without an explicit mapper the command can operate/check addressing on physical segments; no mapper is not by itself a hardware DMA admission failure.

prepare constructs mapArgs with this command, fDevice, alignment, effective bits (0 becomes64), requested prepared length/offset; receives fAlloc/fAllocLength. If returned allocation length differs and is nonzero, it assumes greater length and enters iovmInsert multisegment handling.

Successful mapping stores returned allocation/address+length and marks prepared. Future full-page adapter should return exact supported mapped extent, never arbitrary oversized length to fake success.
kIOMDDMAUnmap calls dmaUnmap when _pages but returns kIOReturnSuccess regardless of its error.

dmaUnmap decrements descriptor DMA reference accounting before calling mapper; mapLength0 skips callback. It updates accounting after mapper return even when unmap failed. These counters do not prove invalidation or backing quiescence.

complete decrements active count; calls unmap then unconditionally clears local allocation address/valid/length and prepared state. clearMemoryDescriptor:455-471 loops complete and releases descriptor. Returning Timeout alone cannot retain reachable backing.

IOGeneralMemoryDescriptor::free can call dmaUnmap without checking its status or complete wired references; IOBufferMemoryDescriptor::free then frees actual buffer. Adapter must hold its own backing/preparation ownership until safe release, or quarantine/fail-stop.

inTaskWithOptions(task,options,capacity,alignment=1) returns caller-owned OSPtr. Allocation may block; default kernel allocation is wired; Pageable requests nonwired; physical contiguous requests may fail/fragment/block. Caller release frees buffer.

inTaskWithPhysicalMask(task,options,mach_vm_size_t capacity,mach_vm_address_t mask) returns OSPtr. Source wrapper passes alignment=1 (cpp:564-575). Public initWithPhysicalMask also exists with explicit alignment.

Unless MapperNone, constructor consults/checks gSystem, which may wait. physicalMask is processed only if alignment<=1, deriving alignment/highestMask then raising alignment to page_size. Direct init with alignment0x4000 plus a physical mask does not enter that mask branch.

Alignment>=page_size rounds capacity; alignment>page_size forces contiguous option. In a global-mapped allocation highestMask can become mapSpecification address-bit restriction and is cleared rather than constraining host physical allocation (295-302).

Nonpageable path sets internal AutoPrepare, allocates wired kernel buffer. HostPhysicallyContiguous forces physical contiguity; PhysicallyContiguous is physical only when no global mapper or MapperNone. Physical restriction path uses IOKernelAllocateWithPhysicalRestrict.

MapperNone prevents automatic/system mapper use for the backing descriptor. getPhysicalSegment(...,MapperNone) requests source physical segments instead of mapped addresses (3694-3719). This is not hardware bypass authorization.

prepare/complete are paired, serialize preparation; prepare may page/wire memory and complete must wait until actual transfer finished. Constructor AutoPrepare exists but explicit client/adapter ownership must still be accounted. Physical-type prepare is trivially successful, not evidence of managed physical allocation.

getBytesNoCopy yields CPU virtual storage. It is not a physical/DMA address. getPhysicalSegment(offset,&length,MapperNone) returns segment plus length, zero at EOF; every page extent needs independent bounds/alignment/reservation checks.

On ARM64 exported PAGE_SHIFT_CONST is runtime data unless private16K definition is active. Do not treat every SDK build as guaranteed16K merely from target triple. Validate actual CPU and DART granules for the initial profile.

setMemoryDescriptor(autoPrepare) and prepare may block and explicitly must not run in gated workloop callbacks/interrupt/spinlock contexts. Separate allocation/preparation/lookup from short publication synchronization.

proposed_minimal_native_contract.status: Proposal/inference from these APIs; not an implemented class or successful DMA contract.
identity_and_publication: One non-system mapper; set inherited fIsSystem=false before base start. Do not copy private reserved layout/fPageSize/fAllocName into the kext.

Provider iommu-id or AAPL,phandle must be exact OSData matching real client iommu-parent. Existing saved design distinguishes DART hardware phandle0x4f from WLAN mapper child0x50 and BT0x51; these are properties, not SID numbers. Validate current real nub/ADT relationship rather than synthesizing authority.

A bounded availability/admission check must precede the indefinite copyMapper path. Publish registerService only after initHardware has genuine exclusive ready hardware ownership, never to satisfy a blocked wait. Keep dependent device bus mastering/DMA gate closed if mapper unavailable.
backing_allocation: First profile only privately owned nonpageable kernel IOBufferMemoryDescriptor full16K pages with no user aliases, explicit allocator failure handling, page-granule and physical-extent verification. Do not accept arbitrary physical descriptors as ownership proof.

For physical table backing, public inTaskWithPhysicalMask(kernel_task, direction|kIOMemoryMapperNone [and explicit host physical contiguity as required], 0x4000, (1ULL<<36)-1) is a candidate allocation path: wrapper uses alignment1 then derives current page size. This is not a tested allocator call, physical/DART admission or blanket recommendation for every payload.

Do not use direct initWithPhysicalMask(...,alignment0x4000,mask36) assuming the mask applies. It bypasses the mask-processing branch in this pin. Do not allow gSystem conversion of PA restriction into IOVA restriction when actual table PAs must fit36 bits.

Retain descriptor and any explicit own prepare reference; enumerate true physical segments with MapperNone and require an entire aligned16K span within verified DRAM and outside every carveout/table/data reservation. Recheck address+length overflow and high physical bits; CPU getBytesNoCopy pointers are never PAs.
Initialize unpublished table RAM explicitly; no API name supplies table-cache coherence, device drain, ownership, invalidation or safe publication.
map_admission: Require a retained explicit correct IOMapper in IODMACommand kMapped; reject missing/wrong mapper before constructor fallback. No kBypassed/kUnmapped/identity fallback.

First bounded restriction may accept only entire owned buffers (offset0,length==descriptor length), all full16K pages; reject partial/subpage/external-UPL/device-memory/fixed-address/identity/paging requests until deliberately implemented. This is a proposed narrow profile, not XNU requirements.

Use independent owned-buffer/requester registry because full-page fast path drops spec.device. Copy and validate ephemeral pageList entries while backing is prepared; do not retain the pageList pointer as lifetime authority. Require pageOffset0 and exact count/length coherence with the actual CPU16K profile.

Allow declared R/W permissions and validated FullyOccupied flag only. Respect numAddressBits/alignment: never shift by64; intersect device ceiling with 32bitIOVA aperture. Physical36bit ceiling remains a separate check. Reject unimplemented options/reserved data rather than silently succeeding.

Own bounded nonreused IOVA reservations and atomic mapping records. Return exact successful mapAddress/mapLength only after table visibility+invalidation complete. Keep caller outputs unchanged on failed adapter transaction as a proposed local guarantee, not an XNU base guarantee.

For first whole-page profile return mapLength==requested length; do not trigger IODMACommand enlarged-allocation iovmInsert fallback accidentally. iovmInsert unsupported forms must return a real error, never success stub.
unmap_and_lifetime: Lookup exact memory/command/base/extent/generation owned record; quiesce requester, revoke mapping, make table updates visible, complete bounded DART invalidation and only then make IOVA/backing reclaimable. Generic complete/unmap return values are insufficient proof.

Own strong retained backing/preparation/table/IOVA records independently of IODMACommand and framework accounting; uncertain hardware-visible publication or invalidation latches fault and retains/quarantines all possibly reachable resources. No reuse/free/rollback claim on timeout.

Do not return success-shaped address from mapToPhysicalAddress for invalid/unknown/quarantined lookup. Its uint64 return has no error channel and callers use it as PA; an explicit containment/fail-stop policy is unresolved and must be settled before real implementation.

Stop/free/unload/sleep/reset cannot free published backing or clear global ownership merely because service is terminating. Retain hardware-visible state until verified quiescence+invalidation, with bounded fail-stop/quarantine policy when those facts cannot be established.

codec_comparison.suitable: Pure exact encoding/whole owned immutable graph validation in ordinary RAM before publication; rejects table/data aliasing and unsupported encodings. No physical allocation or hardware state implied.
codec_comparison.scratch: dld_scratch contains129 byte references and256 uint64 leaf PAs; expected LP64 natural layout2184 bytes (129 rounded to136+2048), not SDK-compiled here. Allocate retained ordinary CPU heap scratch per serialized mapper; do not put the full tables/validator workspace on a callback stack or use device memory as snapshot.
codec_comparison.still_missing: IOVA allocator, own descriptor/preparation registry, locking/publication/cache clean+barriers, DART register reachability/power/lock/stream/RID ownership, fault interrupt, bounded invalidate-complete, transaction drain, reuse/free/quarantine lifecycle. Codec outputs do none of these.

Exclusive WLAN requester/RID2SID/stream and table ownership versus firmware/BT/other clients. ADT mapper-ID match alone does not prove these.
Actual36bit physical backing and tables, complete DRAM/carveout/reservation input and real SDK-visible pageList/UPL ABI.
Hardware table cache maintenance/order, invalidation completion, fault containment, device transaction drain and safe teardown.
Actual subclass SDK linkage/export membership and end-to-end native device DMA; no compiled class, stub, fake-to-real equivalence or hardware bypass supplied.
